nb2c4f43dbef.s: Which of the following pairs (Finance Commission – fact) is correctly matched?
nb2c4f43dbef.x: The 15th FC under N.K. Singh recommended 41%, one point below the 14th FC's 42%.

nindian-polity-26-19.s: The 15th Finance Commission covered which period?
nindian-polity-26-19.x: The 15th FC covered 2020–26 in two reports; 2015–20 was the 14th FC's period.

n0f308e50e77.s: After the 2015 rationalisation, core Centrally Sponsored Schemes are mostly funded in which Centre:State ratio?
n0f308e50e77.x: Core schemes are mostly funded 60:40; the 90:10 ratio applies only to North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

nc3ea14f06f9.s: NEP 2020 set an education spending target of:
nc3ea14f06f9.x: NEP 2020 set an education target of 6% of GDP; 2.5% was the NHP 2017 public health target.

n80bdb55230c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MGNREGA?
o: It provides 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per rural household
Its funding is roughly 90:10 between the Centre and the States
It is confined to urban households
n80bdb55230c.x: MGNREGA concerns rural households, so the last statement is false; the 100 days and the 90:10 funding are correct.

n91f0a977864.s: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to what share of the rural population?
n91f0a977864.x: NFSA covers up to 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population, with 5 kg of grain per person per month.

n7a77f068394.s: JAM-based welfare delivery is criticised because it may:
o: Exclude persons lacking digital access or required documents
Raise the States' share of MGNREGA funding
n7a77f068394.x: JAM streamlines delivery but can exclude those without digital access or documents; it does not eliminate exclusion.

n09a216bf1a0.s: Under the EPC model, who funds the project?
n09a216bf1a0.x: Under EPC the government provides all funding and the private player only constructs.

n5078f789150.s: The Kelkar Committee on PPP recommended discouraging whom from bidding for toll PPPs?
n5078f789150.x: The report proposed discouraging PSUs from bidding for toll PPPs, not barring private participation.

n1370ab46639.s: Outside the roads sector, the Hybrid Annuity Model was pioneered by:
n1370ab46639.x: Namami Gange STPs pioneered HAM outside roads, with performance-linked payments under the One City One Operator model.

nc43cbbc6650.s: Under the Swiss-challenge method, after receiving an unsolicited proposal the Government:
o: Refers it to the Finance Commission
Converts it into an EPC contract
nc43cbbc6650.x: The Swiss-challenge method invites counter-bids after an unsolicited proposal; the Kelkar Committee (2015) discouraged it.

ne4e2925656f.s: In disinvestment, an Institutional Placement Programme (IPP) places shares with:
ne4e2925656f.x: IPP refers to placement only with Qualified Institutional Buyers.

o: Transfers management control to a partner
ndffc3c2c084.x: Minority disinvestment leaves the government above 51% with control; majority disinvestment and strategic sale transfer control.

n64069ebac9c.s: Which of the following is one of the four strategic sector groups under the New PSE Policy, 2021?
n64069ebac9c.x: The four groups are atomic energy, space and defence; transport and telecom; power, petroleum, coal and minerals; and banking, insurance and financial services.

n028421fee8f.s: A statutory body can be altered by:
n028421fee8f.x: A statutory body is created by an Act of Parliament and can be altered by amending that Act.

n23497560da6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about NITI Aayog?
o: The Prime Minister is its Chairperson
Its Governing Council includes all Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of UTs
Its Governing Council consists only of Union Cabinet Ministers and Governors
It was set up by a Cabinet Resolution
n23497560da6.x: NITI Aayog's Governing Council includes all CMs and LGs of UTs, not only Union Ministers and Governors.

n4c8577f7bda.s: Which of the following can a quasi-judicial body do?
o: Exercise the complete jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
Interpret and apply law under statutory authority
n4c8577f7bda.x: A quasi-judicial body is not a court, but it can interpret and apply law, summon persons and impose sanctions under statutory authority.

nindian-polity-65-15.s: Zonal Councils were created under which Section of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
nindian-polity-65-15.x: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under Section 15 of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956; the Inter-State Council rests on Article 263.

nindian-polity-65-11.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is provided for under Article:
nindian-polity-65-11.x: The NCST is under Article 338-A; the NCSC is under 338, the NCBC under 338-B and the linguistic minorities officer under 350-B.

nindian-polity-65-30.s: The State Finance Commission reviews the finances of:
nindian-polity-65-30.x: The State Finance Commission reviews the finances of Panchayats and Municipalities; it is constituted by the Governor.

nca29c49f75d.s: The National Commission for Women is governed by an Act of:
nca29c49f75d.x: The NCW Act is of 1990; 1992 is the NCM Act and 1993 the Protection of Human Rights Act.

n6f17b4102eb.s: The CBI derives its powers from the:
n6f17b4102eb.x: The CBI is non-statutory in itself; it draws its powers from the DSPE Act, 1946 and is associated with the DoPT.

nindian-polity-1-16.s: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
nindian-polity-1-16.x: Sukumar Sen led the Election Commission; M.C. Setalvad headed the first Law Commission of independent India.

nindian-polity-65-13.s: Which of the following is a statutory body, not a constitutional one?
nindian-polity-65-13.x: The CIC is statutory, under the RTI Act, 2005; the ECI (Art. 324) and the Finance Commission (Art. 280) are constitutional.

nab0dc43d009.s: The UPSC annual report is laid before Parliament with a memorandum explaining:
o: Cases where its advice was not accepted
Vacancies in the All India Services
nab0dc43d009.x: Under Article 323 the report goes to the President and is laid before Parliament with a memorandum on non-acceptance of advice.

n1ad45c3837a.s: Annual reports of constitutional bodies such as the CAG, Finance Commission and UPSC are considered by:
n1ad45c3837a.x: Both Houses consider these reports; the Rajya Sabha has equal status with the Lok Sabha here.

n62dc6e19ea0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Planning Commission?
o: It was created by a Government resolution
It was chaired by the Prime Minister
The States were not represented in it
It was a constitutional body under Article 263
n62dc6e19ea0.x: The Planning Commission was an advisory body set up by Government resolution, not a constitutional body.

new.s: The Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) ranking of States is prepared by:
new.x: BRAP state rankings are prepared by DPIIT, first in 2015.

new.s: Which State ranked first in BRAP 2019, released in September 2020?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh was first in BRAP 2019, with Uttar Pradesh second and Telangana third.

new.s: After 1991, States began competing for private and foreign investment mainly because of:
new.x: Post-1991 delicensing made States compete for private and foreign investment.

new.s: Who chairs the 16th Finance Commission (2026-31)?
new.x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC; N.K. Singh chaired the 15th and Y.V. Reddy the 14th.

new.s: The 14th Finance Commission raised the States' share of net divisible taxes:
new.x: The 14th FC raised the States' share from 32% to 42%, a 10-point rise.

new.s: What vertical share did the 16th Finance Commission recommend for the States, as accepted in Budget 2026-27?
new.x: The 16th FC retained the 41% share, accepted in Budget 2026-27; 42% was the 14th FC's share.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT among the four statements laid in Parliament under the FRBM Act?
new.x: The four FRBM statements are Medium-term Fiscal Policy, Fiscal Policy Strategy, Macro-economic Framework and Medium-term Expenditure Framework.

new.s: Under the FRBM Act (amended 2018), Central government debt was to be brought down to what share of GDP by 2025?
new.x: The target was 40% of GDP for Central debt and 60% for general government debt.

new.s: In the GST Council, what share of the votes does the Centre hold?
new.x: The Centre holds one-third of the votes and all States together two-thirds.

new.s: Decisions of the GST Council need a weighted majority of:
new.x: GST Council decisions need a three-fourths weighted majority, so the Centre alone cannot pass one.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the GST Council:
1. It is provided for under Article 279A.
2. It was inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
3. The Centre alone can pass a decision of the Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Council rests on Article 279A (101st CAA, 2016); with only one-third of the votes the Centre cannot pass a decision alone.

new.s: The GST compensation cess was discontinued for most goods from:
new.x: The 5-year compensation ended in June 2022, the cess was extended to repay COVID-era loans, and it was discontinued for most goods from 22 September 2025.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about social sector spending in India:
1. Social protection spending is only about 4.0% of GDP.
2. States bear 75.2% of school education spending.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Social protection is just 4.0% of GDP, and States bear 75.2% of school education spending.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Food Security Act, 2013?
o: It covers up to 75% of the rural population
It covers up to 50% of the urban population
It gives 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month
It gives 10 kg of grain per household per month
new.x: NFSA gives 5 kg per person per month, not 10 kg per household.

new.s: The National Health Policy 2017 set a public health spending target of:
new.x: NHP 2017 targeted public health spending of 2.5% of GDP; 6% is the NEP 2020 education target.

new.s: Direct Benefit Transfer in India began on:
new.x: DBT began on 1 January 2013.

new.s: The VB-G RAM G Act replaced which welfare law?
new.x: The VB-G RAM G Act replaced MGNREGA and raises the States' contribution.

new.s: According to the divergence view, which States attracted most post-1991 private investment?
new.x: The divergence view holds that richer, industrialised States drew most private investment, widening gaps.

new.s: Fiscal transfers try to correct regional imbalances, but disputes arise mainly over their:
new.x: Transfers aim to correct imbalances, but the horizontal criteria for sharing among States spark disputes.

new.s: BOLT stands for:
new.x: BOLT is Build-Own-Lease-Transfer: the asset is leased to the government and then transferred.

new.s: In which PPP model does the private partner design, build, finance and operate the project?
new.x: DBFO(T) is Design-Build-Finance-Operate-(Transfer); EPC is government-funded construction only.

new.s: In 2026 MoRTH raised the net worth requirement for HAM projects to:
new.x: MoRTH raised the HAM net worth requirement to 20% from 15%.

new.s: What is the size of the National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (FY26-FY30)?
new.x: NMP 2.0 is ₹16.72 lakh crore, of which ₹5.8 lakh crore is private; NMP 1.0 was about ₹6 lakh crore.

new.s: Which sector has the largest share in NMP 2.0?
new.x: Highways lead NMP 2.0 with 26%, followed by power 17%, railways and ports 16% each, and coal 13%.

new.s: The National Monetisation Pipeline covers:
new.x: NMP covers brownfield public assets only, with rights given for a limited period; it is not a sale.

new.s: What share does the Centre hold in the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF)?
new.x: NIIF (2015) is a quasi-sovereign fund in which the Centre holds 49%.

new.s: IIFCL (2006) mainly provides:
new.x: IIFCL provides long-term infrastructure debt; VGF gives grants and PPPAC appraises central PPPs.

new.s: Under the VGF scheme, what share of project cost does the Centre normally give as grant for a PPP outside the social sector?
new.x: VGF gives 20% from the Centre plus 20% from the sponsor; 30% + 30% in the social sector.

new.s: In which year did the C. Rangarajan Committee recommend disinvestment of up to 49% in PSUs reserved for the public sector?
new.x: The Rangarajan Committee was in 1993; the Disinvestment Commission under G.V. Ramakrishna came in 1996.

new.s: The Department of Disinvestment, later renamed DIPAM, was set up on:
new.x: The Department of Disinvestment was set up on 10 December 1999 and renamed DIPAM on 14 April 2016.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about DIPAM?
o: It functions under the Ministry of Finance
It manages the Centre's equity in CPSEs
It got its present name on 14 April 2016
It functions under the Ministry of Commerce
new.x: DIPAM is under the Ministry of Finance, not the Ministry of Commerce.

new.s: A Follow-on Public Offer (FPO) in disinvestment is made by:
o: A PSE issuing shares for the first time
new.x: An IPO is a PSE's first issue; an FPO is made by an already listed PSE.

new.s: The first strategic sale, of Modern Foods in 2000, was to:
new.x: Modern Foods was sold to Hindustan Lever (74%) in 2000, the first strategic sale.

new.s: Air India was sold in January 2022 to:
new.x: Air India went to Talace, a Tata Sons company, in January 2022.

new.s: BALCO was strategically sold in 2001 to:
new.x: BALCO went to Sterlite (Vedanta) with 51% in 2001.

new.s: Bhogapuram airport in Andhra Pradesh is being developed by:
new.x: Bhogapuram airport is a GMR project on DBFOT with a 40-year concession.

new.s: Gangavaram Port was acquired by Adani Ports in:
new.x: Adani Ports acquired Gangavaram Port in 2021 and Krishnapatnam Port in 2020.

new.s: Under the Swiss-challenge method, after counter-bids are received the original proponent:
new.x: The Swiss challenge lets the original proponent match the best counter-bid; it is criticised for information asymmetry.

new.s: Aggressive bidding that leads to stalled PPP projects is often called the:
new.x: Aggressive bidding (the winner's curse) and traffic shortfalls stall projects and lead to renegotiation.

new.s: A body created by a resolution or executive order is called:
new.x: Executive bodies rest on a resolution or executive order; constitutional bodies on an Article, statutory ones on an Act.

new.s: Which of the following is a statutory body?
new.x: The NHRC rests on an Act of Parliament; the CAG and FC are constitutional and NITI Aayog is executive.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
new.x: Zonal Councils are statutory; the FC, ECI and Inter-State Council rest on Articles of the Constitution.

new.s: The Chief Election Commissioner is removed in the same manner as:
new.x: The CEC is removed like a Supreme Court judge, not a High Court judge.

new.s: The GST Council was provided for by which Constitutional Amendment?
new.x: The GST Council (Art. 279A) came with the 101st CAA, 2016.

new.s: The Attorney General of India is provided for under Article:
new.x: The AG is under Article 76; Article 165 is the Advocate General, 148 the CAG and 280 the Finance Commission.

new.s: The National Green Tribunal comes under which ministry?
new.x: The NGT (NGT Act, 2010) is under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, not MeitY.

new.s: The Central Vigilance Commission was first set up by a resolution in:
new.x: The CVC was first set up by a 1964 resolution and became statutory under the CVC Act, 2003.

new.s: After 2019, the term of the NHRC Chairperson and members is:
new.x: Since 2019 the NHRC term is 3 years or 70 years of age; earlier it was 5 years.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (body – parent Act) is correctly matched?
new.x: The Press Council Act is of 1978; Lokpal is under the 2013 Act, UIDAI the 2016 Aadhaar Act and the NGT the 2010 Act.

new.s: The Law Commission of India is reconstituted every:
new.x: The Law Commission is constituted by executive notification every 3 years; the 23rd runs from 1 Sep 2024 to 31 Aug 2027.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Law Commission of India:
1. It is a quasi-judicial body.
2. It submits its reports to the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Law Commission is an advisory research body, not quasi-judicial, and reports to the Ministry of Law and Justice.

new.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes were split by which Amendment?
new.x: The 65th CAA created a joint SC/ST Commission; the 89th CAA, 2003 split it into the NCSC and NCST.

new.s: The joint National Commission for SCs and STs was given constitutional status by which Amendment?
new.x: The 65th CAA created the joint SC/ST Commission, later split by the 89th CAA, 2003.

new.s: Before the 102nd Amendment, the NCBC was a statutory body under an Act of:
new.x: The NCBC was statutory under a 1993 Act and became constitutional (Art. 338-B) by the 102nd CAA, 2018.

new.s: The Federal Public Service Commission was set up under the:
new.x: The Public Service Commission of 1926 became the Federal PSC under the GoI Act 1935 and the UPSC in 1950.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Commission for Minorities?
o: It functions under the Ministry of Minority Affairs
It was set up under the NCM Act, 1992
It is a constitutional body under Article 350-B
new.x: The NCM is statutory (1992 Act); Article 350-B is the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

new.s: In which year was the first Public Service Commission set up in India?
new.x: The Public Service Commission was set up in 1926; it became the Federal PSC (1935) and then the UPSC (1950).

new.s: Which of the following has civil court powers such as summoning witnesses and requisitioning records?
new.x: The NCST, NCSC, NCBC and CIC have civil court powers; NITI Aayog and the Law Commission are advisory.

new.s: Which of the following is an example of a quasi-judicial body?
new.x: The Mental Health Review Commission, like the NHRC, SEBI and CIC, is quasi-judicial; the others are advisory.

new.s: State Information Commissions are set up under:
new.x: State Information Commissions are statutory bodies under the RTI Act, 2005.

new.s: A Joint State Public Service Commission is created by:
new.x: Article 315 enables a JSPSC, but the body itself is statutory, created by Parliament.

new.s: Elections to Panchayats and Municipalities are conducted solely by the:
new.x: Local polls are conducted solely by the State Election Commission (Arts. 243-K, 243-ZA), not the ECI.

new.s: Who was the first woman Chief Election Commissioner of India?
new.x: V.S. Ramadevi was the first woman CEC; Sukumar Sen was the first CEC.

new.s: Who was the first Vice-Chairman of the Planning Commission?
new.x: Nehru chaired the Planning Commission with Gulzarilal Nanda as deputy; Arvind Panagariya was NITI Aayog's first Vice-Chairman.

new.s: Under Article 281, the Finance Commission's recommendations are laid before Parliament by the:
new.x: The President lays the FC report before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum, not the Finance Minister.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the report of a Joint State Public Service Commission:
1. It is submitted to each Governor concerned.
2. It is laid before Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: A JSPSC reports to each Governor concerned, and the report is laid before each State Legislature, not Parliament.
